correctness.rationale: The source recurrences reduce exactly under \(g_t=-G\). DoG gives the displayed product, whose logarithm follows from the first two Taylor terms with a summable \(j^{-3/2}\) remainder. DoWG reduces to an autonomous scalar map for \(p_t\); the sign of \(F(p)-p\) is exactly the sign of \(2-p^3-2p^2\), yielding monotone convergence to the unique positive fixed point. The derivative there is strictly below one, which makes the multiplicative ratio errors summable and proves the geometric asymptotic.

value.rationale: The speed at which the learned distance scale escapes a conservative initialization is the central adaptation mechanism of both methods, and the DoWG paper explicitly motivates its weighting as a way to adapt more aggressively. The exact trajectory separation quantifies that motivation on the canonical coherent signal: it changes the growth class and reduces the distance-scale startup cost from quadratic to linear in the logarithm of the unknown distance ratio. The result also explains why pointwise step-size comparison alone understates the feedback effect of the new weighting.
